## Goal

A small end to end report: import, one summary, one plot, and a short conclusion.

## Import and summary

```{r transform}
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr)
enroll <- read_csv("enrollment.csv")

enroll <- enroll |>
  mutate(gpa = na_if(gpa, 999))
```

```{r import}
library(readr); library(ggplot2)
mean(enroll$gpa, na.rm = TRUE)
```

The data has `r nrow(enroll)` students. The average gpa is `r round(mean(enroll$gpa, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`.

## One plot

```{r plot, fig.cap="Distribution of GPA", fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
ggplot(enroll, aes(x = gpa)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "GPA", y = "Number of students")
```

## Conclusion

In conclusion, the histogram shows that the highest amount of students are achieving a 3.5 GPA. The histogram is skewed to the left. There is a presence of low value outliers, causing a tail to the left, towards the lower values.
